summary.headline: Pennar Q4 FY26 PAT rose 14.91% to INR41.04 crores on total income of INR933.7 crores; management commits to 20% PAT growth in FY27.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 total income rose 2.26% to INR933.7 crores while EBITDA grew 15.27% to INR114 crores and PAT grew 14.91% to INR41.04 crores, with PAT margin at 4.44% versus 3.9%. FY26 was a record year: total income INR3,666 crores (up 12.33%), PAT INR138.83 crores (up 16.22%), PAT margin 3.83% versus 3.7%. Management attributed the Q4 revenue slowdown to revenue slipping into Q1 and a solar hit in diversified engineering, and blamed labour shortages for PEB India underperformance in FY26. Working capital rose to 82 days, and gross debt-to-equity rose to 0.98x, both of which management is targeting to reduce.

financial_highlights.change: up from prior level; target 75 days

financial_highlights.value: INR205.57 crores (INR269.93 crores incl. other bank balances)

segments.name: PEB India
segments.commentary: Q4 capacity utilisation at 70%, order backlog INR810 crores (reported as declined QoQ per analyst). Management targets double-digit PEB India growth in FY26 and about 80% utilisation in the year. Labour issues cited as the main FY26 headwind, now resolved.

segments.name: PEB US (Ascent Structural / Telco)
segments.commentary: Management described 'very strong double-digit' Q4 growth in revenue and profitability. Order backlog about $63 million (combined Ascent Buildings and Structurals, with Telco). Backlog reportedly grew about 20% in the last three months.

segments.name: Custom Design Building Solutions (consolidated)
segments.commentary: Revenue rose from INR460 crores to INR516 crores (+12.35%), mainly from the US, driven by the Telco acquisition, partly offset by PEB execution challenges.

segments.name: Diversified Engineering
segments.commentary: Revenue INR429.54 crores; fell due to steel order and BIW weakness, plus a solar revenue hit in Q4. Analyst computed segment margin rising to about 14% from 11.5%, which management attributed to engineering services revenue being booked gross with cost in employee benefits.

segments.name: Engineering Services
segments.commentary: Management reported healthy double-digit revenue and PBT growth in FY26; AI-assisted design and detailing now in use. Analysts were told the segment is not yet at INR100 crores scale.

segments.name: Boilers and process equipment
segments.commentary: Order book increased to INR145 crores (press-stated) or INR128 crores (CFO-stated), with the highest-capacity 100 TPH AFBC and 80 TPH WHR boiler orders secured. Double-digit order backlog growth since March.

segments.name: Hydraulics
segments.commentary: Order backlog about INR34 crores, up from INR22 crores at the prior update; US tariff impact has moderated and orders are returning. European markets being explored.

guidance_outlook: PAT growth of at least 20% in FY27, stated as a firm management commitment; management declined to forecast revenue or EPS growth.
Management did not commit to a large PAT margin jump in FY27; margin expansion to be gradual, quarter-on-quarter and year-on-year.
Working capital to be reduced from 82 days to 75 days in the next few quarters, mainly by cutting inventory and collecting stuck debtors (6 to 8 weeks for handover-linked projects).
Gross debt-to-equity target of 0.8x by end of FY27, through cash generation, founder equity infusion and other board-level options not yet disclosed.
Capex of close to INR100 crores in FY27, mostly completion of the BIW Hyundai plant in 2 to 3 months, followed by automation.
Consolidated tax rate guided at 25% to 26% (about 25.5%). Finance cost guided below 4% of borrowings.
capex_capacity: PEB India capacity utilisation at 70% in Q4; target about 80% in FY27 through added fab and painting capacity.
Capex for FY27 close to INR100 crores, mainly BIW Hyundai plant completion, then automation spend as labour cost arbitrage fades.
US: AGT robotics line commissioned; each robot costs about $200,000 to $300,000; 3 US plants, two of which serve metal building components (Tennessee and Alabama).

Solar JV (minority stake): additional INR5 crores equity to complete the plant, attributed to a USD/INR exposure and a shift to G12R technology. Management said no further capital infusion is planned.
CWIP mainly BIW and repairs and maintenance; annual automation, repairs and maintenance capex close to INR45 crores.
demand_pricing: PEB India: quote activity described as healthy; a INR150 crore order was declined on product-mix grounds. Average order sizes are about INR100 crores for large orders and INR5 to INR10 crores for smaller ones.
Pricing: most of the existing backlog carries price variation clauses. Recent pressure came from steel price increases, which management expects to pass through over time.
Demand verticals: process industries and solar in India; data centres, warehouses and industrial in the US.
US addressable market stated above $10 billion; the company serves the South and Midwest only and has less than 3% share.
Labour: contractor usage increased and automation expanded in painting, surface treatment and assembly; US labour also tighter due to immigration policy.

qa_highlights.question: Why did PEB India order book decline QoQ, and what is the pipeline?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the backlog changes daily and expects it to grow QoQ over the next two quarters; quote activity is healthy and it expects double-digit PEB India growth in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the gross margin jump and is it sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed it to mix: higher value-add in BIW, ICD and boilers, and engineering services; margins guided at a similar 42% to 43% level.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management committed to at least 20% PAT growth, not EPS growth, given possible equity dilution; it declined to guide revenue.

qa_highlights.question: Is labour still an issue, and what was the revenue shortfall in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said labour is resolved and not expected to recur in the medium term, and that the Q4 shortfall was revenue slipping into Q1, not labour supply.

qa_highlights.question: What is the debt plan and why did gross debt-to-equity rise from 0.78x to 0.98x?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the rise to the Telco acquisition and seasonal working-capital borrowing at year-end; target is 0.8x by year-end FY27, with board options not yet disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Iran war or energy inflation affecting the outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said cost increases have been passed on to customers, the company has modelled them, and it sees no impact on revenue or margin plans beyond energy price risk.

qa_highlights.question: What is the legacy business share and its growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Legacy businesses are 30% to 35% of revenue; management said prioritised business units are growing faster, and the overall growth rate divided by 0.7 gives their rate.

qa_highlights.question: What are the US margin and scale prospects?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed high US costs to senior management and engineering talent; operating leverage expected as Telco and Ascent Structurals reach higher utilisation.

risks_watch: Gross debt-to-equity at 0.98x against a 0.8x target; working capital at 82 days against a 75-day goal, with about INR60 to 70 crores of excess India working capital.
Debtor collection: management said stuck debtors depend on handover of pending project sites within 6 to 8 weeks.
Steel and commodity price increases (management cited INR10,000 per tonne) and the pace of pass-through to customers.
Labour cost inflation and automation spend, with management acknowledging a margin compromise for now.
Possible board-level corporate action and founder equity infusion, with no details yet; land parcel monetisation also under consideration.
PEB India utilisation (70%) and order backlog trend needed to reach the 80% target and double-digit growth.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the FY27 PAT growth commitment and margin trajectory, but cautious on the balance sheet, where management conceded 0.98x debt-to-equity is 'not a number we are comfortable at'. Evasive on revenue guidance, on the board's corporate action options and on the size of the land monetisation. Some answers were inconsistent on figures (order book and segment numbers).
key_quotes: We are committing that as a management team, we are committed to 20% PAT growth.
0.98 is not a number we are comfortable at. 0.8 we'll commit to as a management team.
Labor issues have now been resolved, and we do not believe we will have a recurrence in the medium term of this issue.
We cannot swallow INR10,000 increase in our commodity pricing on a per ton basis nor can we swallow a 10% increase in our operating costs, right?

adds.what: BIW Hyundai plant completion (diversified engineering), capex part of ~INR100 crore FY27 capex
PEB India added fab and painting capacity to lift utilisation to ~80% (no capacity size given)
US AGT robotics line (commissioned; automation, not a capacity addition in size)

growth.why: Management firmly commits to at least 20% PAT growth in FY27 but declines to guide revenue or EPS; backing is partial, citing PEB India utilisation rising toward ~80% via added fab and painting capacity, a PEB India backlog of INR810 crore, a US backlog of about $63 million, and price variation clauses, with no revenue number given.
